user.title: Swiss Solar Forecast
user.description: Where is the plant, and what does the module plane look like? Your Home Assistant location is pre-filled; move the marker or search for a place or postal code. One entry is one plane: set up a second entry for a roof facing another way. Azimuth is the compass bearing the modules face (0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west); tilt is the inclination from horizontal. Losses cover wiring, inverter, soiling and mismatch (14 % is a usual figure). The inverter limit clips the AC power (0 = none). Damping scales the result, for calibration against your real yield.

reconfigure.title: Move the plant
reconfigure.description: Move the marker or search for another place or postal code; the forecast point is then picked in the next step. The entry keeps its entities, their ids and history. The plane itself is changed in Configure.

init.title: Module plane
init.description: Peak power, orientation, tilt, losses, inverter limit and damping of this plane. Changing a value reloads the entry; entity ids and history are kept. Use damping to calibrate: if the forecast is 10 % too high over a few sunny weeks, set 0.9.

forecast_unreachable.title: Swiss Solar Forecast: forecast not readable
forecast_unreachable.description: The MeteoSwiss open data could not be read for several refreshes in a row ({error}). Check your internet connection; if it is fine, the MeteoSwiss service is down or has changed. The sensors stay unavailable until then and recover on their own; this notice disappears with the next successful refresh.
